subject: Performance follow-up: context limits, streaming & capacity plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance follow-up: context limits, streaming & capacity plan

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

Recap & requirements we captured on the call:
- Latency SLO target: p95 ~ 250ms for short responses (<=512 output tokens). For longer responses (~1500 tokens) we are seeing acceptable p95 up to ~450ms if streaming is enabled.
- Context shape: typical prompts are 1k-4k tokens; worst-case single request could be up to ~6k input tokens. Expected output per request between 200–1.5k tokens depending on use case.
- Throughput/concurrency: initial pilot expects ~100 requests/minute with bursts to 100 concurrent open sessions; long-term target discussed at 30–50 concurrent active users.
- Streaming: required for progressive user experience on long summaries; ability to start sending tokens within ~100–200ms of first token generation is important.

Risks we flagged:
- Very large input windows (>=6k) increase per-request latency non-linearly due to kv-cache and attention costs.
- High concurrency with long outputs can push GPU memory and reduce effective batching efficiency.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the latency SLOs above and share a representative sample of prompt+expected output length distributions.
2) We'll produce an SLO options matrix (latency vs cost vs model variant) and a recommended canary configuration for a 2-hour pilot.
3) Internal action: draft cost estimate and Dedicated vs Hosted pilot tradeoffs (Marissa + Ben).
4) Schedule a canary window next week — propose Thu 09:00–11:00 PST; confirm if that works for Acme.

Attachments: acme_perf_summary_v1.pdf (initial notes)

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance follow-up: context limits, streaming & capacity plan

Great summary — thanks Rachel.

Couple clarifications from our engineering side:
- For our ’clinical summarization’ flow we typically generate ~1.2–1.6k tokens per call on average; occasionally up to ~2k.
- We really want streaming for these flows — clinicians expect partial results within a couple hundred ms to start rendering.
- Target concurrency for Pilot A is ~40 sustained sessions, with spike testing up to 100 concurrent.
- Latency SLO: we'd prefer p95 <= 300ms for short responses, but we can tolerate up to 500ms for the long streaming responses as long as partial chunks arrive continuously.

I've attached a short trace and a sample batch of prompts (we'll upload full prompt set to Drive once we sanitize PHI).

-- Emily

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme perf follow-up — ops recommendations & asks

Team — internal plan after Emily's clarifications:

Recommended pilot config:
- Use Dedicated pool (reserved) to guarantee capacity for the canary window; 2x gpu nodes with 48GB each as baseline.
- Model variant: production-safe 13–16B open model with quantized execution; fall back to smaller 7B for extreme concurrency.
- Serving config: dynamic batching with small max_batch_time (6–8ms) and aggressive prefix KV caching for repeated prompts.
- Max token enforcement: enforce per-request ceiling at 8k (input+output) and surface hard error vs truncated output options.
- Streaming: enable chunked streaming with initial flush target <=200ms from generation start; tune chunk size to 64–128 tokens.

Action items:
- Marissa: prepare a cost delta table (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a committed-capacity recommendation.
- Ben: produce a canary runbook with synthetic traffic shape (mix of short, medium, long) and success criteria.
- Laura: prepare an eval prompt set to monitor quality regressions during model fallbacks.

Attachments: slo_options_matrix.xlsx (SLO vs cost table)

I will send a proposed canary schedule once costs are available.

Rachel
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Short update — cost estimate and canary window.

- Cost: baseline Dedicated pilot (2x48GB nodes) estimated monthly pro-rata incremental of ~$5,800 for the pilot day (includes burst GPU credits); Hosted incremental for same profile ~30% higher at current rates.
- Canary window: Thu 2026-07-29 09:00–11:00 PST confirmed from our side.
- Success criteria proposed: p95 <= 300ms for short responses, streaming partials must begin within 250ms for long summaries, error rate <0.5% under spike test.

Emily — can you confirm you will provide:
1) sanitized prompt set or a sanitized subset by Mon 07/26
2) a synthetic traffic file (CSV) describing arrival rates and token distributions

Once we have those, Ben will coordinate the canary run.

Thanks — Ben
